## Fatal finding

- **`thm-closed-real-function-algebras-are-function-spaces-on-their-quotients` — Statement and proof step 2.2.** The theorem includes \(X=\varnothing\) but claims an **isometric** algebra isomorphism. Step 2.2 defines the relevant distance using
  \[
  \sup_{x\in X}|g(q_A(x))-h(q_A(x))|.
  \]
  For \(X=\varnothing\), both this and the corresponding supremum over \(Y_A=\varnothing\) are \(\sup\varnothing\), which is undefined under the library’s real-supremum convention. The library explicitly states that its uniform metric requires a nonempty domain and that “for \(X=\varnothing\) … \(\sup\varnothing\) is undefined” in [the uniform-metric lemma](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/lem-uniform-metric-on-a-function-space.md:42). The parenthetical “the empty case is the unique-function case” in [step 2.2](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-closed-real-function-algebras-are-function-spaces-on-their-quotients.md:58) proves the algebraic bijection but does not equip the singleton function spaces with a metric. Thus the [Statement’s isometry claim](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-closed-real-function-algebras-are-function-spaces-on-their-quotients.md:26) needs \(X\ne\varnothing\) or an explicit empty-domain metric convention. **Severity: fatal** because the Statement covers the empty compact Hausdorff space.

No other fatal or nonfatal defect found.

Coverage: I read all seven assigned items fully, both page files, every relevant boundary row in the batch proof contract, and all fourteen immediate dependency/citation targets fully. I additionally checked the empty-function and uniform-metric convention clauses. The empty function is indeed simultaneously the zero and constant-one function; the \(M=0\), \(m=M\), singleton, \(n=0\), and \(n=1\) branches are otherwise sound. The AI-generated finite-space example survived the empty, singleton, complex non-self-adjoint, and finite-topology tests, and it is not a dependency target. Nothing required by the dispatch was left unchecked.
